status: measured and recorded. This round is primarily a RETRACTION: the central empirical claim of R1M, R1N and R1O -- that the GF(16) subgroup ladder splits into collapsing and non-collapsing rungs, with the break between GF(4) and GF(16) -- does not survive a relabelling of the modes and is not a fact about the field. Two candidate replacement rules were fitted and one of them also failed out of sample. The surviving mechanism is stated with its weak direction marked weak.

withdrawn_clauses: rule C's WEAK direction, recorded below as 'zero crossing pairs -> collapse ... 9 of 9'. Refuted at the first cut it had not seen: M3 at split 2 has zero crossing pairs and does not collapse.

the phrase 'out_of_sample_weak_direction'. The three families supporting it were constructed at the same single cut the rule was defined against, so they were not out of sample in the respect that mattered.
supersession.what_still_stands: the retraction itself -- the collapse dichotomy is a labelling artifact, 9 of 9 against 0 of 72 -- the orbit geometry of Part One, the failure of the Pauli centre rule, the failure of the same-qubit count, and rule C's STRONG direction.
supersession.the_repair: zero crossings is necessary and not sufficient; the family must also cover every mode within each block. M3 never heralds mode 0 because 0 is the fixed point of multiplication, and M3 + (0,1) collapses to exact zero at every seed.

subject: src/aionq/pond.py::relabelling_report, ::cut_crossing_pairs, ::same_qubit_pairs, ::pauli_centre_rank and src/aionq/gf_frames.py::orbit_geometry_report
the_question_that_prompted_it: the user asked what relationship governs the orbits of x -> x^2 against the orbits of x -> w x, and suggested the link might lie in the stabiliser group each pair family generates inside the Pauli group. Both halves were computed. The first has a clean answer. The second is the rule that failed.

part_one_the_orbit_geometry.statement: pass GF(16)* to the exponent coordinate Z/15 by discrete log. There x -> w x is a TRANSLATION and x -> x^2 is a DILATION -- the additive and the multiplicative structure of one and the same line.

measured.dilation_normalises_translation: sigma M_a sigma^-1 = M_{a^2}, verified for all fifteen a

part_one_the_orbit_geometry.the_single_intersection: <2> preserves <5> setwise, so the M3 orbit {0,5,10} -- which is GF(4)* -- is a union of Frobenius orbits, {0} and {5,10}. It is the only M3 orbit that is, and correspondingly the two rungs share exactly ONE mode pair out of 19 and 15: (2,3), inside GF(4). The subfield is the whole intersection.
part_one_the_orbit_geometry.why_R1P_could_not_see_it: both rungs have six orbits including zero -- five 3-cycles against sizes 1,1,2,4,4,4 -- so every count-based invariant R1P tried gives them the same value. The difference is in the shape, not the count.
part_one_the_orbit_geometry.what_it_does_not_do: it does not explain the collapse dichotomy, because by Part Two there is no field fact there to explain.

part_two_the_retraction.what_was_claimed: R1M: 'the break in the field tower is between GF(4) and GF(16)' -- T2, T4 and FROBENIUS drive the entropy to exactly zero, M3, M15, T16 and AGL do not, and this was read as a statement about which subgroups of AGL(1,16) close.
part_two_the_retraction.the_test: a relabelling permutes the modes. It leaves the pair set, the graph it forms, its component count, its F2 rank, its Pauli centre and every other intrinsic invariant unchanged -- it only renames modes. If the field structure were doing the work, the collapse would survive.

measured.design: 3 collapsing rungs x (identity + 8 random relabellings) x 3 storm seeds, 150 steps each, n = 8 qubits

part_two_the_retraction.verdict: the collapse dichotomy of R1M through R1O is an artifact of the mode-to-qubit labelling. R1M's own typed remainder named this risk in the exact words 'identifying mode j with field element j is a choice the Jordan-Wigner ordering fixes; the rungs act on those labels, so a relabelling conjugates them', and it went untested for three rounds while three further findings were built on top of it.
what_survives_from_R1M_to_R1O: every state in every storm stays exactly Gaussian -- that is a statement about the operations, not the labelling
the storm is a sink toward stabiliser states
weak and projective heralds differ in KIND: asymptotic decay against arrival in seven steps and freezing. Measured at one labelling but the mechanism is the alpha -> pi/4 limit, not the labels
the break-count continuity in the measurement strength
what_is_withdrawn: 'the break in the field tower is between GF(4) and GF(16)'
'collapse is about the family being closed under a subgroup'
the reading of T2/T4/FROBENIUS versus M3/M15/T16/AGL as a property of those subgroups

rule_a_the_pauli_centre.the_users_suggestion: the stabiliser group each pair family generates inside the Pauli group
rule_a_the_pauli_centre.computed: even-weight Majorana monomials c_S, c_T anticommute exactly when |S intersect T| is odd -- c_S c_T = (-1)^(|S||T| - |S intersect T|) c_T c_S with both weights even -- so two edge generators anticommute exactly when the edges share a vertex. The radical of the induced symplectic form on the F2 edge span is the centre of the generated group.
rule_a_the_pauli_centre.a_prose_slip_in_this_manifest_before_com: the first draft of this entry and of the two docstrings wrote the condition as |S symmetric-difference T| odd, which for two 2-element sets is always EVEN and so would say no two edges ever anticommute. The code was right throughout -- it computes bin(u & v).count('1') & 1, the intersection parity -- and only the prose was wrong. Recorded because a wrong statement of a rule beside a correct implementation of it is how a reader ends up trusting the wrong one.
rule_a_the_pauli_centre.in_sample: PERFECT separation over all ten families -- radical 4 or 8 for every collapsing family, 0 or 1 for every other.
rule_a_the_pauli_centre.out_of_sample: FAILED on the first family it was not fitted to. A random perfect matching has radical 8, identical to T2, and gives final entropy 2.0 at three seeds.
rule_a_the_pauli_centre.why_it_is_recorded: a rule that separates every point it was built on and then breaks on the first new one is the exact failure mode this repository keeps finding, and the near-miss is more informative than the miss.

rule_b_the_same_qubit_count.the_reading: under Jordan-Wigner mode j lives on qubit j//2, so i c_2k c_2k+1 is the single-qubit Z on qubit k. T2 is translation by 1, which pairs x with x^1 -- the same qubit. T2's eight pairs ARE the eight single-qubit Z measurements.
rule_b_the_same_qubit_count.that_part_stands: it is a complete account of what T2 is at the identity labelling, and T4 contains all eight.

the_general_rule_fails.FROBENIUS_relabelled_with_4: final entropies 2.0, 1.0, 1.0 -- a HIGHER count and no collapse
the_general_rule_fails.eight_Zs_plus_eight_crossing_pairs: the maximum count of 8, final entropies 3.0, 1.0, 1.0 -- no collapse

rule_b_the_same_qubit_count.verdict: the same-qubit count is not the mechanism. The first draft of this round's docstrings said it was.

rule_c_the_cut.statement: entanglement_entropy reads the MIDDLE CUT, so on eight qubits the cut falls between mode 7 and mode 8. A herald on a pair that does not straddle it is local to one side, and local operations cannot build entanglement across it.
rule_c_the_cut.separation: exact over all ten families, and it also accounts for the control that destroyed rule A: a random perfect matching has four crossing pairs.
rule_c_the_cut.out_of_sample_strong_direction: crossing pairs -> no collapse. Confirmed on a family carrying all eight single-qubit Z's plus eight crossing pairs, at three seeds: 3.0, 1.0, 1.0.
rule_c_the_cut.out_of_sample_weak_direction: zero crossing pairs -> collapse. Tested on three random block-diagonal families with ZERO same-qubit pairs, three seeds each. Seven of nine reach exact zero at 150 steps; the two that do not read 0.918 and 0.806 at 150 and exact zero at both 400 and 900, so those two are step budget and not exceptions. 9 of 9. See the remainder: checked on three constructed families, not proved.
rule_c_the_cut.the_step_budget_control: the budget cuts one way only, and that was checked rather than assumed. Relabelled families run to 900 steps do NOT drift to zero: T2 relabellings freeze at 2.0, 3.0, 2.0 and FROBENIUS relabellings at 2.0, 3.0, 3.0, identical or higher than at 150. So the 0-out-of-72 of Part Two is not itself a budget artifact -- which is precisely the trap R1O fell into and had to correct.
rule_c_the_cut.why_it_is_a_mechanism_and_not_a_lookup_t: it names a causal path -- local operations do not create entanglement across the cut they are local to -- and it predicts the sign of a family it was not built from. The four invariants R1P tried named none.
rule_c_the_cut.and_it_is_still_about_the_labelling: which pairs cross depends entirely on where the modes sit relative to mode 8. That is the labelling. So rule C explains the collapse WITHOUT rescuing any claim about GF(16).

what_is_not_claimed: that zero crossing pairs implies collapse. Three constructed families and nine runs support it; it is not proved and the two slow runs needed 400 steps.
that the orbit geometry of Part One bears on hardness, entanglement or the collapse. It is a statement about GF(16) and Z/15 and nothing measured connects it to the storm.
that any earlier round's Gaussianity results are affected. Those are statements about the operations and are labelling-independent.

that the relabelling test exhausts S_16. Eight relabellings per rung out of 2.1e13, chosen at random. The result is one-sided -- zero collapses out of seventy-two -- so it refutes 'the collapse is intrinsic' without measuring how rare the collapsing labellings are.

typed_remainders.statement: the weak direction of rule C -- zero crossing pairs implies collapse -- rests on three constructed families at three seeds, 9 of 9, with two runs needing 400 steps rather than 150. A family with zero crossings that provably never collapses would refute it and was not searched for. Nor was the obvious sharpening measured: whether the surviving entropy of a crossing family is a function of the crossing count.

the cut is the middle cut because entanglement_entropy chooses it. Every result in R1M through R1Q is relative to that choice; a different bipartition gives a different crossing count and, by rule C, a different dichotomy. No round has varied the cut.

R1M, R1N and R1O are not deleted and their manifests still assert the field-tower reading in their own text. This manifest supersedes those specific claims; the earlier files have not been rewritten, so a reader who finds R1M first will find a withdrawn claim stated as a finding.

Part One answers what relates the two orbit systems and stops there. Whether the semidirect product GammaL(1,16) = Z/15 : Z/4 has any measurable consequence in this repository -- a rung between M15 and AGL, a herald family, anything -- was not tested. It is the natural next rung of the ladder and it is not this round's.

Built and measured by the Claude session on the Linux container. Witness-nerve rank 0: verifier equals producer. Three rounds of findings were built on a claim whose own remainder named the test that refutes it, and the test cost four minutes of compute.
